### LOW: Revision\-only mode ignores the \`promote\` input and always promotes
[\.github/workflows/register\-model\.yml:192](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/da7a5b6c78e1cbca54c47ca026d0fbc5d3bf3156/.github/workflows/register-model.yml#L192) · T-012, T-027

In \`publish\_revision\_only\` mode, the payload at lines 190\-192 contains only \`version\` and \`hugging\_face\_artifact\`\. The \`promote\` input is dropped, and the input description says the mode will 'Publish and promote'\. An operator who sets \`promote=false\` together with \`publish\_revision\_only=true\` expecting a staged\-only publish therefore sends a request that, per the documentation, promotes the revision\. Promotion changes the manifest providers download and verify \(A\-004, T\-027, T\-012\) and is meant to need specific approval\. The workflow has no environment or approval gate; a single publishing key is enough, and the script does not validate that \`version\` matches a reviewed upload\. Fix: reject \`promote=false\` when \`publish\_revision\_only\` is set, or send an explicit promote flag and let the backend honour it\. Put the job behind a protected GitHub environment with required reviewers\. Also require a non\-null pinned \`hugging\_face\_artifact\` or document what null does to an existing pinned source\.

Raised by: anthropic/claude\-sonnet\-5\.5

### LOW: Registration no longer documented as verifying file hashes; integrity rests on provider\-side checks
[docs/operations/model\-migration\.md:142](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/da7a5b6c78e1cbca54c47ca026d0fbc5d3bf3156/docs/operations/model-migration.md#L142) · T-012, T-027

The runbook previously said HandleRegisterModel verified that every listed file exists with the declared size and hash\. It now says the handler only validates identity and declared inventory and checks listed file sizes, and that providers verify hashes at download time\. Step 1 also lets operators skip upload and reuse an already\-published manifest\. A mismatched, corrupted or substituted object under the CDN prefix could then be registered and promoted with no coordinator\-side content check\. The alias fan\-out would push that build to the fleet, and each provider's hard\-swap is the only point where the bytes are checked\. The trigger is a publishing mistake or CDN/R2 tampering\. The impact is fleet\-wide failed prefetches and retry load, or a stale or incorrect weightHash in the catalog\. A malicious provider could also exploit a weak catalog hash to pass the weight\-hash routing gate \(T\-027, T\-012, SEC\-007\)\. The threat model and A\-004 notes still describe coordinator weight\-hash verification and have not been updated\. The fix is to update the threat model, or restore hash verification at registration\. Otherwise the runbook should require a pre\-register hash audit and a single\-provider canary before any promote or alias flip\.

Raised by: anthropic/claude\-sonnet\-5\.5
